meters.headline: Inline electromagnetic flowmeter.
meters.principle: A conductive liquid moving through the meter’s magnetic field induces a voltage at the electrodes. The transmitter converts that signal into velocity and volumetric flow. The full-bore tube has no moving measuring parts; the liquid must fill it completely.
features: Integral and remote transmitter options let you position the display for access and the process environment.
Forward, reverse and net totalisers support bidirectional measurement. Empty-pipe detection, flow direction and fault diagnostics help with commissioning and operation.
Choose the lining, electrodes and process connection together for the liquid chemistry and operating duty.
meters.care: Inspect the liner and electrodes for coating, abrasion or chemical attack. Check grounding, zero, flow direction and output scaling during verification. Request the supplied meter’s calibration record and set a periodic verification schedule for the application.
meters.confirmation: Liquid conductivity must be above 20 µS/cm. Temperature, lining, pressure and connection options must be specified together; maximum limits are not automatically available in one assembly.

meters.name: EcoFlow
meters.description: A lightweight plastic-body meter for compatible conductive liquids, with a remote transmitter.
meters.imageAlt: Illustration of an EcoFlow plastic-body flowmeter and remote transmitter
meters.fit: Up to 5 kg/cm² and 55 °C. Check chemical compatibility with both HDPE and the SS316L electrodes.
meters.installation: Support the pipe on both sides of the flanges, keep the tube full and confirm grounding. Check the process stays inside the pressure and temperature limits.

meters.headline: Plastic-body electromagnetic flowmeter.
meters.method: Electromagnetic measurement in an HDPE tube
meters.principle: Electrodes detect the voltage generated as a conductive liquid moves through a magnetic field. EcoFlow uses a molded HDPE measuring tube without a separate liner, connected to a remote transmitter for flow indication and output.
features: A lightweight HDPE body and flow tube suit compatible conductive liquids within the stated pressure and temperature limits.
The remote transmitter keeps the local display accessible, with a standard cable between sensor and transmitter.
Check the electrodes as well as the body: the standard wetted electrodes are SS316L, so chemical compatibility depends on both materials.
meters.care: Inspect the HDPE body, flange supports and electrode condition. Verify grounding, full-pipe operation, zero and output scaling. Check for deposits and follow a cleaning method compatible with both HDPE and SS316L.
meters.confirmation: Confirm the minimum liquid conductivity for the supplied model. The HDPE body and SS316L electrodes must both suit the liquid; verify the complete assembly’s pressure rating and flange dimensions.

meters.name: SonicLine
meters.description: Transit-time measurement for suitable conductive and non-conductive liquids, with an unobstructed bore.
meters.imageAlt: Illustration of a SonicLine inline ultrasonic sensor and wall-mounted transmitter
meters.fit: Liquid viscosity up to 350 cSt. Standard process limits: 40 bar and −20 to 200 °C; confirm the combined duty.
meters.installation: Install the inline sensor with a full bore and adequate straight pipe. Plan the initial installation separately from transducer servicing; live service requires the appropriate fittings and procedure.
keyFacts: 4–20 mA, pulse, relay; HART / PA options

meters.headline: Inline ultrasonic flowmeter.
meters.method: Transit-time ultrasound through a dedicated flow tube
meters.principle: Transducers send sound upstream and downstream through the liquid. Flow changes the travel time in each direction; the transmitter uses the difference to calculate velocity and volumetric flow. The acoustic path allows measurement of suitable conductive and non-conductive liquids.
features: Two acoustic paths are standard, with a four-path configuration available on request.
An unobstructed measuring bore and a separate wall-mounted transmitter provide process measurement and accessible local indication.
Transducers can be replaced under pressure only with the specified retractable fittings and service procedure. Plan the initial inline installation separately.
meters.care: Verify signal quality, zero and the configured flow range during commissioning and periodic checks. Inspect electrical connections and the process assembly. Under-pressure transducer work requires the correct service fittings, procedure and trained personnel.
meters.confirmation: These are standard-configuration limits. Flow range depends on size; verify acoustic suitability and combined pressure, temperature, material and interface requirements for the selected assembly.

meters.name: ClampWave
meters.description: Transit-time flow measurement from outside an existing pipe, with no wetted sensor parts.
meters.imageAlt: Illustration of ClampWave external transducers clamped to a pipe and connected to a transmitter
meters.fit: The pipe must run full and transmit a usable acoustic signal. Select sensors for its material, wall thickness and temperature.
meters.installation: Prepare the pipe surface, apply the specified coupling material and set transducer spacing from the actual pipe dimensions. Verify signal quality; aeration, solids, scale and lining need an application check.

meters.headline: Clamp-on ultrasonic flowmeter.
meters.method: Transit-time ultrasound from outside the pipe
meters.principle: Two external transducers send ultrasound through the pipe wall and liquid in opposing directions. The difference in travel time gives flow velocity; the transmitter uses the entered pipe dimensions to calculate volumetric flow. Sensors remain outside the process.
features: Add flow measurement to an existing full pipe without cutting or draining it. There are no wetted sensor parts.
Choose wide-beam, universal or high-temperature sensors for the pipe material, dimensions and process conditions.
The single-channel transmitter provides local indication, totaliser control inputs and plant interfaces, with microSD and USB service access.
meters.care: Check coupling material, transducer contact and mounting stability. Recheck spacing and pipe settings after a sensor is moved. Compare signal quality and flow readings during periodic verification; aeration, solids, scale and pipe lining can affect the acoustic path.
meters.confirmation: The stated 1% accuracy applies at velocity ≥0.3 m/s. Pipe-size coverage depends on sensor selection. Transmitter temperature limits do not establish the process-temperature rating of the selected sensors.

meters.name: EchoFlow
meters.description: Measures liquid level above a flume or weir, then derives flow from its head–discharge relationship.
meters.imageAlt: Illustration of an EchoFlow ultrasonic transmitter mounted above an open channel
meters.fit: Flow range and accuracy depend on the flume or weir, its geometry and the configured head–discharge curve. The level range is not a flow range.
meters.installation: Mount vertically with the required beam clearance at the primary device’s specified head-measurement point. Confirm the flume or weir geometry, level reference and flow conversion before use.

meters.headline: Non-contact ultrasonic flow transmitter.
meters.method: Pulse-echo level measurement, converted to flow
meters.principle: A transducer mounted above the liquid sends an ultrasonic pulse and times its returning echo. This gives the distance to the surface and the liquid level. At a flume or weir, the configured head–discharge relationship converts the measured head into flow.
features: The transducer measures from above the channel without contacting the liquid.
A correctly specified primary device, such as a Parshall flume or a V-notch or rectangular weir, provides the relationship between head and flow.
Local indication and the selected plant interface carry level, calculated flow and totalised volume. False-echo suppression helps distinguish the surface from fixed obstructions.
meters.care: Keep the transducer face and acoustic path clear. Check the measured level against a reference, inspect the flume or weir for deposits or damage, and verify the head–discharge settings. Foam, vapour and obstructions require a signal check under actual operating conditions.
meters.confirmation: The range, resolution, repeatability and accuracy below describe level measurement. Flow range and accuracy depend on the flume or weir, its geometry, condition and configured head–discharge relationship.
